title: Add CLI/MCP engine selection knobs
description:
Background: The planning doc calls for CLI flags and MCP knobs so users can choose the voice engine (`local` vs `cloud`) and urgency profile. This bead ensures `briefly` exposes the necessary arguments and persists the choice for future runs.

Tasks:
- Add `--voice`/`--engine` flags to `BriefCommand` that default to `local`. Interpret `voiceMode` preferences (auto/always/never) documented in `voice-mode-setup.md`.
- Introduce environment variables (`VOICE_ENGINE`, `VOICE_PROFILE`, `STT_PROFILE`) and config keys so CI/cron runs can pin a preferred stack.
- Ensure the MCP server honors the engine selection via shared configuration (update `brieflyMCPServer` to accept the same settings).
- Write a CLI validator that warns when the local MLX stack is unavailable and automatically switches to `cloud` if `mlx-audio` health check fails.

Success criteria:
- `briefly brief --engine local` uses the new defaults and `--engine cloud` uses the legacy fallback.
- Environment variables can override the CLI flags.
- CLI help text and docs mention the new options and reference the plan doc for context.

title: Benchmark + document the local voice path
description:
Background: The beads workflow must end with verifying and documenting the new voice stack (per planning doc). We also need a benchmark story that demonstrates the latency/cost advantages versus ElevenLabs.

Tasks:
- Create `briefly voice benchmark` command that runs a standard prompt through the local engine, records time-to-first-audio + CPU/memory, and writes JSON + Markdown summaries to `logs/voice-benchmark.md` + `logs/voice-benchmark.json`.
- Update `README.md`, `docs/plans/MLX_VOICE_UPGRADE.md`, and `docs/voice-mode-setup.md` to describe the new MLX default, CLI flags, fallback path, and the research sources that justify Kokoro+Parakeet+Smart Turn.
- Document how the Swift refactor keeps the `VoiceEngine` module inside `briefly` and how to tie it to the `local-voice-system` MLX infrastructure (link to `projects/local-voice-system/MLX_VOICE_PLAN.md`).
- Capture testing instructions (unit tests for engines, benchmark command, Smart Turn behavior) inside a new doc `docs/plans/LOCAL_VOICE_TESTS.md`.

Success criteria:
- Documentation references the research and plan, the fallback path is clear, and the new benchmark command outputs both JSON and Markdown for later comparison.
- Tests exist (or are tracked) for engine selection, Smart Turn detection, and CLI flag parsing.
- README includes quickstart for installing `mlx-audio`, running the server, and toggling `voice_mode` preferences.

title: Refactor BriefService around VoiceEngine
description:
Background: BriefService currently contains ElevenLabs-specific voice code. The plan calls for a soft cascade (local MLX voice engine → fallback) and for the voice selection to be configurable via environment/CLI flags.

Tasks:
- Inject `VoiceEngine` into `BriefService` via initializer (default parameter referencing config). Keep the existing logic for the `BriefService` workflow, but swap direct `sag` calls for `voiceEngine.synthesize(...)`.
- Introduce `VoiceUrgency`/`VoiceProfile` settings so the service can request Kokoro (`normal`) vs LFM 2.5 (`premium`) depending on the urgency.
- Ensure the Smart Turn hook can signal `BriefService` when a voice interaction finishes so we can stop streaming audio earlier.
- Add metrics/logging around which engine is selected (write to `logs/voice-engine.log`).

Success criteria:
- `BriefService` compiles and defaults to `MLXVoiceEngine` while still accepting `ElevenLabsVoiceEngine` via a public initializer.
- Voice urgency config is documented and toggles the proper model names.
- Logs include an entry each time `voiceEngine` is invoked, noting the selected profile and latency.

title: Integrate Smart Turn + voice loop
description:
Background: Smart Turn v3.x is the semantic VAD we rely on (per plan and research). The Swift voice loop must consume Smart Turn signals to break streaming at the right time and avoid extra latency.

Tasks:
- Add a `SmartTurnAnalyzer` wrapper (Swift/CLI) that listens to the Parakeet stream or the MLX server, emits `finished` markers, and exposes them to `BriefService` via async continuations.
- Integrate the analyzer with the voice engine so the CLI/voice loop stops recording as soon as Smart Turn signals completion, reducing dead air.
- Add logging/metrics for false positives (tracked via `smart_turn.log`) and allow overrides (`SMART_TURN=off` or `VOICE_MODE=legacy`).
- Provide fallback to plain silence detection if Smart Turn is unavailable (e.g., `mlx-audio` not running).

Success criteria:
- Smart Turn analyzer compiles, runs in the background, and notifies the voice engine of user turn completion.
- The voice loop uses Smart Turn to minimize response latency (<200ms after user stops speaking).
- Logs highlight Smart Turn decisions and fallback activation when necessary.

title: Introduce VoiceEngine abstraction & MLX connector
description:
Background: The planning-workflow doc (docs/plans/PLANNING_WORKFLOW_BRIEFLY_LOCAL_VOICE.md) calls for a native Swift VoiceEngine that defaults to the MLX stack, uses Kokoro/Parakeet/Smart Turn, and keeps ElevenLabs as a fallback. We will reuse the GabGab/MLXVoice library so the new engine is built on `MLXVoiceSessionManager` rather than re-implementing HTTP/multipart plumbing.

Tasks:
- Create `Sources/brieflyCLI/Voice/VoiceEngine.swift` with an async `synthesize(text:urgency:output:)` protocol.
- Implement `MLXVoiceEngine.swift` as a thin wrapper around `MLXVoiceSessionManager` from `/Volumes/Main SSD/Developer/GabGab/MLXVoice`, exposing TTS, STT, health checks, and Smart Turn hooks.
- Add `ElevenLabsVoiceEngine.swift` (legacy path) that wraps the existing `sag` calls via the shared `ShellExecutor` so the protocol is satisfied.
- Wire the new module into the package manifest (`Package.swift`) and export the namespace so SwiftPM can resolve the local `MLXVoice` dependency.

Success criteria:
- `VoiceEngine` protocol compiles and exports from the CLI module.
- `MLXVoiceEngine` can call `http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech` and transcribe via Parakeet for a simple text sample by delegating to `MLXVoiceSessionManager`.
- `ElevenLabsVoiceEngine` reuses the existing scripts so `briefly --engine cloud` remains a drop-in.
